decision_conditions: Details of the front boundary treatment shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The front boundary treatment shall be erected in accordance with the approved detail before the development is occupied.Reason: To ensure satisfactory appearance and safeguard the privacy, amenity and safety of adjoining occupiers and the public and in the interests of highway safety.

The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the end of three years from the date of this permission. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:Location and Block Plans E00 21.01.2026Existing Drawings Floor Plans E01 20.01.2026Existing Drawings Elevations E02 20.01.2026Existing Drawings Elevations E03 20.01.2026Existing Drawings Section E04 20.01.2026Proposed Location and Block Plans P00 12.02.2026Proposed Drawings Floor Plans P01 12.02.2026Proposed Drawings Elevations P02 12.02.2026Proposed Drawings Elevations P03 12.02.2026Proposed Drawings Section AA P04 12.02.2026Proposed Drawings Details P05 12.02.2026Highway Safety Impact FormSuDS Pro FormaReason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied by more than SIX residents at any one time. Reason: To ensure that the future occupation of the building does not adversely affect the adjoining premises/immediate.

No independent cooking or laundry facilities shall be installed in any of the respective bedrooms and the communal kitchen and dining/living rooms shall be retained in perpetuity. Reason: To accord with the stipulations of definition as a House of Multiple Occupation and to safeguard the residential character of the surrounding area.

Prior to occupation; unless otherwise agreed; cycle parking should be provided in compliance with the following criteria:i) Provision of a minimum of SIX long stay cycle parking spaces one per HMO bedroom.ii) In an accessible location; the access route to each long stay store should be a minimum of 1.2m wide to enable the bike to enter the store, should be step free and involve no more than 2 doors or gates [excluding the store door] which must also have a minimum opening width of 1.2m.iii) Secured with a British standard mortice lock or a fob.iv) Fully enclosed: 4 walls and a roof.Such facilities to be retained permanently thereafter.Reason: To ensure the provision and availability of adequate cycle parking.

Notwithstanding the approved plans, prior to first occupation of the development hereby permitted, details of the design and siting of refuse storage facilities including facilities for the recycling of waste to satisfy the future number of occupiers on site, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, in accordance with the Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (2024). Once approved the development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details prior to first occupation and retained for the lifetime of the development. Reason: In order to facilitate efficient, safe and clean removal of household refuse, the location and accessibility of refuse storage plus to maintain safety on the Highway.

All new external work shall be carried out in materials that resemble, as closely as possible, in colour and texture as specified in the approved application.  Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.
description: Change of use from Use Class C3 (dwelling house) to Use Class C4 (HMO-house in multiple occupation) with associated cycle and refuse storage and rear dormer with outrigger dormer and front rooflights.
